summary: Describes how to carry IPv6 over Near Field Communication, which links devices a few centimeters apart, using an adaptation layer. It helps devices like phones use IPv6 over NFC links.

eli5.summary: Phones that touch can talk with a short-range radio. This explains how to make the internet's newer addresses work over it.

questions: how to send ip packets over near field communication
how does ipv6 work over nfc
what is the mtu for ipv6 over nfc
what is miux in nfc llcp
subtitle: How phones and other devices that touch each other can carry IPv6 packets over Near Field Communication.

tldr.problem: Near Field Communication links devices only centimeters apart, but those devices still want Internet connectivity, and IPv6 has no defined way to ride on NFC.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reuses 6LoWPAN techniques over the NFC peer-to-peer mode and its Logical Link Control Protocol (LLCP): a 6-bit link address becomes the basis for the IPv6 interface identifier, headers are compressed, and the link is configured for a 1280-byte MTU so no fragmentation is needed.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that lets an NFC-enabled device act as a 6LoWPAN node (6LN) talking to a border router (6LBR), or form an isolated NFC network.

today: RFC 9428 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2023, and no RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why Put IPv6 on NFC
sections.content:
Near Field Communication (NFC) is a set of short-range wireless technologies, typically needing 10 cm or less between sender and receiver. It operates at 13.56 MHz at rates from 106 kbps to 424 kbps. An NFC exchange always has an initiator and a target; the initiator generates a radio field that can power a passive target, so tags, stickers, key fobs and cards need no battery.

RFC 9428 says it is desirable for NFC-enabled devices to support IPv6 because of its large address space and its tools for unattended operation. It specifies this using 6LoWPAN techniques from RFC 4944, RFC 6282 and RFC 6775, because 6LoWPAN was designed for IEEE 802.15.4 networks whose characteristics resemble NFC.
sections.eli5: Tiny gadgets and phones that touch want to join the internet too. This RFC borrows tricks made for tiny low-power networks to let them do that.

sections.title: The NFC Peer-to-Peer Stack
sections.content:
NFC defines three modes of operation: card emulation, peer-to-peer and reader/writer. Only peer-to-peer mode lets two devices exchange information in both directions, so it MUST be used for IPv6 over NFC.

On top of the NFC physical layer sits the logical link layer, built on the Logical Link Control Protocol (LLCP). The LLCP has Link Management, Connection-oriented Transmission and Connectionless Transmission parts. An IPv6 packet MUST be passed down to the LLCP and carried in the Information field of an LLCP Protocol Data Unit (I PDU). The LLCP does not support fragmentation and reassembly. Between LLCP and IPv6 sits an IPv6-LLCP Binding and the IPv6-over-NFC adaptation layer.

The adaptation layer provides Neighbor Discovery, stateless address autoconfiguration, header compression and fragmentation and reassembly, all based on 6LoWPAN. 6LoWPAN header compression does not define compression for TCP, so TCP still works over NFC, only without that optimization.
sections.eli5: Only the mode where both devices can talk back and forth is used. A thin translation layer sits between the internet language and the NFC radio, like an interpreter between two people.

sections.title: Link Addresses and IPv6 Addresses
sections.content:
NFC devices identify service access points with two kinds of 6-bit addresses, the SSAP (source) and the DSAP (destination). The IPv6-LLCP Binding MUST pass these to the adaptation layer. Values 0x2 through 0x3f are assigned by the local LLC as a result of an upper-layer service request, so those values can be used to generate IPv6 interface identifiers (IIDs).

An NFC device performs stateless address autoconfiguration per RFC 4862. IIDs for all unicast addresses are 64 bits long and built with the stable random identifier algorithm of RFC 7217. The NFC SSAP MUST be a source of that algorithm's Net_Iface parameter, because a bare 6-bit address is short and easy to scan. The algorithm uses SHA-256, and the secret key SHOULD be at least 128 bits and MUST be initialized to a pseudorandom number.

The link-local address is formed by appending the IID to the prefix fe80::/64. Where a 16-bit short address is needed, it MUST be formed by padding the 6-bit NFC SSAP to the left with zeros.
sections.eli5: Each device has a very small number as its link name, which would be easy to guess. So the device mixes it with a secret to make a longer, hard-to-guess internet address.

sections.title: MTU and the MIUX Parameter
sections.content:
The Information field of an I PDU is limited by the Maximum Information Unit (MIU). Its default is 128 octets. A device may announce a larger value by sending the optional MIUX parameter, and the MTU is then calculated as MTU = MIU = 128 + MIUX.

The MIUX parameter is a TLV with Type 0x02 and Length 0x02, and its value is encoded in the least significant 11 bits of the Value field. The maximum possible value is 0x7FF, which gives a maximum LLCP MTU of 2175 bytes. To meet the IPv6 minimum MTU of 1280 bytes, the MIUX value MUST be 0x480.

Because the link can carry that MTU, IPv6 over NFC MUST NOT use fragmentation and reassembly at the adaptation layer.
sections.eli5: By default NFC can carry only small envelopes. The devices agree to use big envelopes instead, so no letter ever has to be cut into pieces.

sections.title: Neighbor Discovery, Compression and Multicast
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery follows RFC 6775. A 6LoWPAN node directly connected to a border router MUST register its address by sending a Neighbor Solicitation with the Extended Address Registration Option (EARO), and Duplicate Address Detection is not required in that case.

Encapsulated datagrams start with a one-octet dispatch value. The only sequence defined is the LOWPAN_IPHC compressed IPv6 header (dispatch pattern 01 1xxxxx) followed by the payload. All headers MUST be compressed per RFC 6282, and implementations MUST also support Generic Header Compression (GHC) from RFC 7400.

The NFC link layer does not support multicast, so packets are always unicast. If a border router needs to multicast to its nodes, it replicates the packet on each link, which costs power. So the border router MUST track multicast listeners per NFC link and MUST NOT forward multicast packets to nodes that have not registered for the group. A node that wants to send multicast unicasts the packet to the border router.
sections.eli5: Devices sign in with the group leader, shrink the labels on every message, and since NFC can only talk to one neighbor at a time, the leader sends group messages only to those who asked for them.

sections.title: Connectivity Scenarios
sections.content:
In the first scenario, an NFC device (a 6LN) talks over an NFC link to a 6LoWPAN border router (6LBR) that is connected to the Internet. The distance is typically 10 cm or less. The RFC's example is a laptop connected by Wi-Fi or Ethernet that also supports NFC and acts as the 6LBR. Several 6LNs may connect to one 6LBR, each connection using a different IPv6 prefix, and the 6LBR MUST ensure address collisions do not occur.

In the second scenario the NFC network is permanently isolated. In multihop topologies a 6LoWPAN router (6LR) can do the same tasks as the border router, and Duplicate Address Detection needs the multihop extensions of RFC 6775.
sections.eli5: A touching phone can connect through a laptop to the whole internet, or a few devices can just form a tiny private club with no outside connection.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery in unencrypted wireless networks may be open to the threats in RFC 3756. The RFC then summarizes what the NFC LLCP specification provides: protection of user data through encryption with a secret key established during link activation, and two secure-transfer modes. Ad hoc mode needs no prior knowledge of the partner but can be vulnerable to on-path attacks; authenticated mode protects against them.

NFC is considered by many to have intrinsic security because of its short range. For address privacy, IPv6 over NFC uses a random stable identifier as the IID, NFC applications use short-lived connections, and a different address is used for each connection. This mitigates correlation of activities, location tracking and address scanning.
sections.eli5: Being close helps keep things private, and the link can also scramble messages. Devices also change their internet address for each short chat so nobody can follow them around.
